t.E417.agn: The SCF (1992) and JECFA (1987) had set the ADI as 'not specified'; in 2017 EFSA saw no need for a numerical ADI and found no safety concern for the general population at the reported uses. No adverse effects were reported at the highest doses in long-term animal studies.
t.E417.body: Tara gum is not absorbed intact in the gut; it is expected to be fermented by bacteria in the large intestine.
t.E417.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E417.prod: Obtained by physical means from plant seeds or tree exudate (gum).
t.E417.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern for the general population.
t.E417.regx.1: Group I additive; may not be used in jelly mini-cups or in dehydrated foods intended to swell with water when swallowed.
t.E417.summary: A plant gum obtained from the seeds of the tara tree. It thickens ice cream and sauces.
